Lenacapavir for prevention of HIV acquisition

In the two phase 3 lenacapavir prevention trials, what is the incidence of HIV acquisition with lenacapavir relative to the randomised oral active control, and separately relative to the background incidence estimated in the screened population?

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: Report each trial separately; compute NO pooled estimate

Cochrane Handbook sections: 10.3.3, 10.8, 10.4.4, 10.10.1, 10.10.3

One reason is sufficient and it is arithmetic rather than judgement: Purpose 1's rate ratio is exactly zero, so it has no logarithm, and the generic inverse-variance method that sections 10.3.3 and 10.8 prescribe for combining rate ratios operates on log ratios. There is nothing to give it. Section 10.4.4 is cited for what it actually covers -- rare events in two-by-two data, where it recommends the Peto method and warns that adding a half to each cell 'usually has the undesirable effect of biasing study estimates towards no difference'. That warning is about cells and these are rates, so it is cited as the nearest guidance rather than as governing; a reviewer objected to an earlier version that cited it as though it governed, and was right. A Peto odds-ratio synthesis on the participant counts IS computable and is not performed for two stated reasons: it would silently change the estimand from the rate ratio both trials published to an odds ratio on participants, and both trials allocated unequally, which is the condition 10.4.4 identifies as biasing that method. The population difference between the trials is recorded as clinical diversity under 10.10.1 and is not claimed to be independently sufficient -- an earlier version did claim that, which is stricter than the Handbook, since 10.10.3 treats declining to synthesise as a judgement about whether an average would mislead and random-effects models exist precisely to carry such diversity.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: Report each trial separately; compute NO pooled estimate, and never combine this with the randomised contrast

Cochrane Handbook sections: 3.2.3, 10.3.3, 10.8, 10.10.1

The comparator is not a randomised group. Section 3.2.3 distinguishes the kinds of comparison a review may make, and an estimate against an incidence modelled in a screened population is not the same quantity as a contrast between two randomised arms: it carries the assumptions of that model and none of the protection randomisation provides. The two are reported as separate outcomes for that reason. No synthesis across trials is computed here either, and the governing reason is the same arithmetic one as for the randomised contrast -- one trial's rate ratio is zero and the generic inverse-variance method of 10.3.3 and 10.8 has no log ratio to take. An earlier version invoked that reason here while citing only the comparison-definition and heterogeneity sections, which did not govern it.

  1. No GRADE assessment or reconciliation record is held in this object, so the certainty of this evidence has not been rated. This is recorded as a declared departure under Cochrane Handbook §III.3.4.1: the review reports a pooled estimate for which no certainty assessment was made. Rating it here would require two assessors and an adjudicator, and a rating produced by neither is not a GRADE assessment whatever letter it carries.
  2. Read this beside `whether the estimand was established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the same quantity. It records nothing about what that quantity was measured against -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

Paper

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

Lenacapavir for prevention of HIV acquisition1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. title

Abstract

Question. In the two phase 3 lenacapavir prevention trials, what is the incidence of HIV acquisition with lenacapavir relative to the randomised oral active control, and separately relative to the background incidence estimated in the screened population?1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. question

Introduction

Background. This review asks: In the two phase 3 lenacapavir prevention trials, what is the incidence of HIV acquisition with lenacapavir relative to the randomised oral active control, and separately relative to the background incidence estimated in the screened population? It examines 2 randomised trials and does not pool them. The outcomes sought are Lenacapavir against F/TDF, the randomised active control; Lenacapavir against the estimated background incidence in the screened population; F/TAF against F/TDF, both randomised oral arms; F/TAF against the estimated background incidence.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. manuscript.introduction

Methods — search

Primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. bookkeeping_2026_08_21.the_search_its_date_and_its_databases

Methods — outcomes sought at every registered rank

Every registered rank -- primary, secondary and other -- was read for 2 of 2 contributing trials before any decision about which outcomes could be combined; each records the time it was read.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. inputs.trials[].all_ranks_read_utc

Methods — synthesis

Intervals are 95% confidence intervals.1

Methodological decisions follow Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al (editors). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5 (updated August 2024). Cochrane, 2024., version 6.5 (updated August 2024), and the sections relied on are listed in the object rather than cited generically.2

Sources for this section (2)
  1. config.confidence_level
  2. methodological_authority.reference

Limitations

3 claim(s) previously made about this review were corrected and the corrections are retained on the object rather than overwritten.1

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.2

  2. results.by_outcome

The underlying records are the 4 source(s) listed under References; each names the layer it was read at, so a reader can tell a registry record from a published report.1
